Subject: TIA scope + subprocessor encryption attestation for Aeterna telemetry

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking this on. We have a couple of specific asks as we prepare to move telemetry (diagnostic events that may include limited identifiers) into Redwood-managed ingestion for our EU product lane. Legal is calling this a TIA scope question and they want confirmation on two items before we can proceed: 

1) Intended scope of the TIA/DTIA for transient telemetry — will Redwood treat telemetry as "processing" that requires SCC coverage, or does the transient/ephemeral nature permit a narrower technical safeguard approach? We need the wording so our privacy counsel can map it to our DPA.

2) Subprocessor encryption attestations — a handful of our third-party SDKs forward traces to Redwood via your ingestion. Can you provide an attestation that all subprocessors engaged in storage or transit of these telemetry blobs either (a) encrypt at rest and in transit using customer-keyed KMS, or (b) are covered by contractual safeguards (SCC + UK IDTA addendum) and provide an internal encryption attestation?

Attached is our preliminary inventory of fields we classify as telemetry (see attachment: subprocessor-map.csv). Can you confirm what evidence you need from the Redwood side and whether you can accept a consolidated attestation versus individual subprocessors providing separate forms?

We are targeting a compliance checkpoint with our counsel by EOW next week, so a two-week turnaround would be ideal.

Best,
Michael Turner
Head of Privacy, Aeterna Diagnostics

Hi Michael — thanks for the clear ask and the inventory. Short answers up front: we can support SCC coverage and a UK IDTA/UK Addendum flow where required, and we can produce a consolidated encryption attestation for the set of Redwood-managed subprocessors. A few clarifying points below so we scope the evidence properly.

What we can provide from Redwood:
- A consolidated attestation covering: at-rest encryption algorithms, TLS v1.2+ for transit, KMS custody model, and key rotation cadence for Redwood-managed keys.
- Subprocessor list export (CSV) with hosting region, role (transit/storage/processing), and legal entity.
- Where a subprocessor is customer-keyed (BYOK), we can provide evidence of key usage policies and the KMS integration doc.

Questions for Aeterna (quick):
1) For the telemetry you shared, do you consider the payloads to be "personal data" under your DPA classification? If yes, we will treat them as in-scope for SCC/UK addendum mapping.
2) Do you require customer-keyed KMS for storage in any region (e.g., EU)?
3) Any subprocessors on your map that require token redaction before delivery to Redwood?

Next steps I propose:
- I will attach a TIA evidence checklist (spreadsheet) and a preliminary subprocessor export — please validate the mapping.
- Kim (cc) will confirm the contractual route (SCC vs. additional UK Addendum language) and whether Redwood's consolidated attestation suffices for Aeterna's counsel.
- Marissa will coordinate a short working session if you prefer a live walkthrough.

I have attached our TIA-evidence-checklist.xlsx for your intake. If you confirm that telemetry is personal data in your classification, we'll start the SCC/IDTA mapping and return a redlineable attestation within ~7 business days.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Policy & Privacy Lead
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Proposed contractual approach + fallback routing

Team — quick note laying out the legal stance we should offer Aeterna and the operational fallback we will propose: 

Legal approach (me):
- If Aeterna classifies telemetry as "personal data" -> propose SCCs for processor relationships + UK IDTA (UK Addendum) where UK residents are implicated. This aligns with our standard DPA addendum. We'll provide a consolidated attestation signed by Redwood Legal covering all current subprocessors.
- If telemetry is non-personal (per their counsel) -> we can issue a technical safeguards statement (encryption in transit/at rest, retention windows) but avoid SCC mapping.

Operational fallback (Jonas / infra):
- For EU traffic we can enforce region-based routing to EU-only pools by creating an ingestion route flagged in tenant config. For a transient telemetry SLA, we propose a 7-day retention default; anything longer triggers BYOK requirement.
- If Aeterna requires customer-keyed KMS, we'll run a scoped BYOK onboarding (2-3 week ops work) and provide an interim mitigant (additional access logging + separated KV namespaces) until keys are onboarded.

Attachments to prepare for external send: routing-diagram.png (simple lane diagram), proposed attestation text (I will draft), and a redlineable SCC mapping doc. I suggest we propose an initial action plan: intake validation (3 business days), attestation draft (5 business days), DocuSign signature window (5 business days).

LMK if timing looks tight. We should be conservative with dates for procurement.

Kim
Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

- Our counsel confirmed the telemetry contains limited identifiers and will be treated as personal data for EU residents. Please proceed with SCC + UK Addendum mapping.
- We prefer a consolidated attestation to simplify procurement review. If Redwood can name the subprocessors and certify encryption coverage on their behalf, that should be sufficient — we do not need individual subprocessor forms.

Two operational asks:
1) Can Redwood indicate which subprocessors are US-hosted (we have a strict routing preference that those payloads be pseudonymized before crossing the Atlantic)? If so, please mark them in the CSV.
2) We have one subprocessor (LogiCache) that will insist on separate contractual addenda. Can you note in your attestation that LogiCache is a special case and propose an orchestration plan (either separate NDAs or a LogiCache attestation) so our procurement can close?

I have started a DocuSign envelope with our counsel and appended the intake spreadsheet: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/ABC123456789. We will aim to sign within five business days after Redwood shares the attestation draft.
